note: Read off the detail sheets of 0359342_PDF_Edition_Sunglasses_Stand_REV_4.pdf. Pages 8-28 are one part per sheet and the title block names the part. Each entry carries a basis: absent means 'read' (printed on the sheet, rank 72 — a DXF or a model still beats it); 'inferred' means worked out from what the sheet shows, with the working stated, and ranks below every measurement. Every fabricated part in the pack is priced. MBY433 is the only one absent and that is not a gap: it is the Prong Assembly of MBY432 + MBY434, so it has no blank of its own — its money is the puddle weld and dress, x56. Quantities are not stated here; the roll-up is in the NOTES file. Where a provisional MAKE METHOD is assumed, it is written into read_from, and the labour it implies is called out as NOT included in the material figure.

JAE823.read_from: page 11 prints the FINISHED tray, not a flat pattern: plan 650 x 550, sides 95 high, returns 24, R14 typ, 6mm Corian. Developed blank inferred as 650 + 2x95 + 2x24 = 888 by 550 + 2x95 + 2x24 = 788. This is thermoformed solid surface, so the sheet is bought at the developed size and formed. Confirm against the former. Note the sheet is stamped DETAIL FOR REFERENCE ONLY, and the finish is 800-grit all faces, no visible swirl. Provisional method: buy one 888 x 788 sheet of 6mm Corian per part (no nesting assumed — solid surface is bought to size), heat and vacuum-form over a former, trim the 24 returns, then 800-grit all faces with no visible swirl. FORMING, TRIMMING and the 800-grit finishing are NOT in the material figure; nor is the former. Waste: the developed rectangle already includes the returns, so allow normal solid-surface offcut on top

JAE824.read_from: page 12 prints a solid block 40 x 40 x 50 high, material 'MDF' with no gauge. 50mm exceeds any board on this job, so it is laminated up or cut from thick stock. Priced as a 40 x 40 x 50 solid so the line is not empty; the make method drives the real cost and needs confirming. Provisional method assumed for pricing: laminate three 18mm MDF boards to 54mm and machine back to 50, rather than buy 50mm stock — 40 x 40 is small enough that bonding offcuts is cheaper than a thick-stock purchase. BONDING and the machining to size are NOT in the material figure. If SDI would rather buy thick stock, the purchasing basis changes and so does the price
